Project Overview

A portfolio solution scenario for consistent incident routing, using issue categories and subcategories to identify an appropriate support group.

Business Scenario

Incoming incidents require consistent routing to the appropriate support group based on the nature of the issue.

03

Requirements

  • Evaluate incident category and subcategory against a clear set of routing conditions.
  • Identify a support group for known issue combinations and provide a fallback for unmatched incidents.
  • Preserve intentional manual assignments and avoid repeated reassignment.

Solution Design

Detailed Workflow / Architecture

08

Implementation Approach

  1. 01

    Agree on a routing matrix

    Define category/subcategory mappings and a fallback with support teams. Store target groups as references in configuration, with active flags and explicit precedence.

  2. 02

    Start with Assignment Rules

    Use native Assignment Rules when conditions express the routing clearly. They apply to unassigned tasks; overlapping rules need deliberate ordering because the lowest matching order takes precedence.

  3. 03

    Use a Business Rule only for the custom path

    For a maintained lookup model, a before-insert Business Rule can query a custom mapping table using GlideRecord. Guard preassigned records, set assignment_group on current, and avoid current.update() inside the rule.

  4. 04

    Notify after a meaningful assignment

    Configure the notification for a newly assigned group or a real group change, rather than sending an email every time an incident is saved.

09

Technical Logic

Configurable group references

The lookup stores a reference to sys_user_group. Environment-specific records may not share the same sys_id, and group names can change. Move or reconcile configuration deliberately instead of embedding identifiers or display names in scripts.

Safe lookup behavior

Filter by category, subcategory, and active status. Require one unambiguous result and an active target group. An absent or ambiguous result should take a defined fallback path.

Update policy

The sample only handles insertion. Re-evaluation after category changes needs a separate explicit rule that respects manual ownership and avoids reassignment loops.

Configuration-based routingjavascript

Synthetic server-side example for a before-insert Business Rule. u_portfolio_route and its fields are illustrative custom configuration, not built-in tables. Fallback handling is outside this focused fragment; this is not employer code or a drop-in production rule.

// Demonstration only; custom schema must be defined first.
(function routeIncident(current) {
  if (!current.assignment_group.nil() || !current.assigned_to.nil()) return;

  var route = new GlideRecord('u_portfolio_route');
  route.addQuery('u_active', true);
  route.addQuery('u_category', current.getValue('category'));
  route.addQuery('u_subcategory', current.getValue('subcategory'));
  route.setLimit(2);
  route.query();
  if (!route.next()) return; // Use the configured triage path.

  var groupId = route.getValue('u_assignment_group');
  if (route.next() || !groupId) return; // Ambiguous or incomplete.

  var group = new GlideRecord('sys_user_group');
  if (!group.get(groupId) || group.getValue('active') !== '1') return;

  current.setValue('assignment_group', group.getUniqueValue());
  // A before rule persists this value without current.update().
})(current);
10

Technical Challenges & Decisions

Rules versus a lookup table

Use declarative rules for a small stable matrix. Use a governed lookup when many mappings need ongoing maintenance; restrict who can edit that configuration.

No hard-coded sys_ids

Keep group choices in reference fields owned by configuration. The script then reads the configured reference and validates it, without baking one instance's identity into source code.

No competing writers

Do not let an Assignment Rule, Business Rule, and flow all set assignment_group independently. Document execution order and choose one owner for each scenario.

11

Testing Approach

Proposed validation scenarios and expected results for an isolated ServiceNow test environment.

Each synthetic routing mapping
The correct active group is selected for software, network, and hardware cases.
Group already assigned
The existing assignment remains unchanged.
Missing or duplicate lookup rows
No arbitrary group is selected; the controlled fallback/triage path runs.
Inactive target group
Assignment is not made to the inactive group.
Repeated unrelated updates
No reassignment loop and no duplicate assignment notifications.
